vectors.title: Vectors
vectors.objective: Add and scale vectors componentwise and compute a vector's length.
vectors.query: vector components scalar multiplication addition length magnitude norm

problems.prompt: Let u = (1, 2) and v = (3, 5). Compute u + v.
problems.format: Enter the components separated by commas.

signatures.note: multiplied matching components instead of adding them

problems.hint: Vector addition is componentwise: add the first components, then the second components.
problems.explanation: Add matching components: (1 + 3, 2 + 5) = (4, 7).

problems.prompt: Compute 3 times the vector (2, -1).
problems.format: Enter the components separated by commas.

signatures.note: added 3 to each component; scalar multiplication multiplies every component

problems.hint: A scalar multiplies every component.

problems.prompt: What is the length (magnitude) of the vector (3, 4)?

signatures.note: summed the components; length is the square root of the sum of squares
forgot the final square root (25 is the squared length)

problems.hint: Square each component, add the squares, then take the square root.

problems.prompt: Let u = (3, -1, 4) and v = (1, 2, -2). Compute 2u - v.
problems.format: Enter the three components separated by commas.

signatures.note: added v instead of subtracting it (sign slip)
computed u - v; the scalar 2 was never applied to u

problems.hint: Compute 2u first, then subtract v one component at a time.

dot_product.query: dot product inner product multiply components sum orthogonal perpendicular angle

problems.prompt: Compute the dot product of (1, 2) and (3, 4).

signatures.note: listed the componentwise products without adding them

problems.hint: Multiply matching components, then add the products. The result is one number.

problems.prompt: Compute the dot product of (2, 0) and (5, 7).

signatures.note: listed the componentwise products without adding them

problems.hint: Multiply matching components, then add the products.

listed the componentwise products without adding them

problems.prompt: For what value of k are the vectors (1, k) and (4, -2) orthogonal?

signatures.note: solved 4k - 2 = 0; the second components pair as k times -2
orthogonal means the dot product is zero; k is not just the other vector's component

problems.hint: Orthogonal vectors have dot product zero. Write the dot product and solve for k.

matrix_multiplication.title: Matrix Multiplication
matrix_multiplication.objective: Know when AB exists, what shape it has, and how each entry is computed.
matrix_multiplication.query: matrix multiplication rows columns inner dimensions product entry

problems.prompt: A is a 2 by 3 matrix and B is a 3 by 4 matrix. What are the dimensions of AB? Give rows, then columns.

signatures.note: reported the inner dimensions; the result keeps the outer dimensions
gave columns then rows; the question asks rows, then columns

problems.hint: The inner dimensions must match and disappear; the outer dimensions give the shape.
problems.explanation: (2 by 3) times (3 by 4): inner 3 and 3 match, so AB is 2 by 4.

problems.prompt: Can a 2 by 3 matrix be multiplied by another 2 by 3 matrix?
problems.format: Answer yes or no, optionally with a reason.

signatures.note: the inner dimensions (3 and 2) must match

problems.hint: Compare the number of columns of the first matrix to the number of rows of the second.
problems.explanation: No. The first matrix has 3 columns but the second has 2 rows; the inner dimensions must match.

problems.prompt: Let A = [[1, 2], [3, 4]] and B = [[5, 6], [7, 8]]. What is the entry in row 1, column 1 of AB?

signatures.note: multiplied matching entries instead of taking a row-by-column dot product
paired row 1 of A with a row of B; use a column of B

problems.hint: Take the dot product of row 1 of A with column 1 of B.
problems.explanation: Row 1 of A is (1, 2); column 1 of B is (5, 7). 1*5 + 2*7 = 19.

problems.prompt: Compute AB for A = [[1, 2], [3, 4]] and B = [[5, 6], [7, 8]]. Give the four entries row by row.
problems.format: Enter four numbers separated by commas.

signatures.note: multiplied matching entries (elementwise) instead of row-by-column
listed the entries column by column; the question asks row by row

problems.hint: Each entry is a dot product of a row of A with a column of B.

eigenvalues.title: Eigenvalues
eigenvalues.objective: Recognize eigenvalues and eigenvectors and compute eigenvalues of small matrices.
eigenvalues.query: eigenvalue eigenvector characteristic equation determinant trace diagonal

problems.prompt: What are the eigenvalues of the diagonal matrix [[2, 0], [0, 3]]?
problems.format: List every eigenvalue, separated by commas.

signatures.note: added the eigenvalues; each one should be listed separately
the off-diagonal zeros are not the eigenvalues; the diagonal entries are

problems.hint: For a diagonal matrix the eigenvalues are the diagonal entries.
problems.explanation: A diagonal matrix has its eigenvalues on the diagonal: 2 and 3.

problems.prompt: In one sentence: what does it mean for v to be an eigenvector of A with eigenvalue lambda?

signatures.note: mixes up eigenvectors with the trace, determinant or diagonal entries
signatures.example: v is the diagonal of A with trace and determinant

problems.hint: Think about what A does to v: is the result in the same direction?
problems.explanation: A v is a scalar multiple of v, A v = lambda v, with v nonzero: A only scales v and keeps its direction.

problems.prompt: A = [[4, 1], [0, 2]] is upper triangular. What are its eigenvalues?
problems.format: List every eigenvalue, separated by commas.

signatures.note: the eigenvalues of a triangular matrix are the diagonal entries, not the off-diagonal ones
gave the trace (the sum of the eigenvalues); list each eigenvalue

problems.hint: For a triangular matrix, read the eigenvalues off the diagonal.
problems.explanation: A triangular matrix has its eigenvalues on the diagonal: 4 and 2.

problems.prompt: Find the eigenvalues of A = [[2, 1], [1, 2]].
problems.format: List every eigenvalue, separated by commas.

signatures.note: used the trace and determinant directly as eigenvalues; they are the sum and product
diagonal entries are eigenvalues only for triangular matrices

problems.hint: The trace is 4 and the determinant is 3. Solve lambda^2 - 4 lambda + 3 = 0.
problems.explanation: lambda^2 - 4 lambda + 3 = (lambda - 1)(lambda - 3) = 0, so the eigenvalues are 1 and 3.

big_o.title: Big-O Notation
big_o.objective: Read the growth rate of simple loops and expressions and state it in Big-O form.
big_o.query: big-o notation growth rate complexity loops nested dominant term

problems.prompt: What is the Big-O time complexity of summing the elements of a list of n numbers?

signatures.note: every element has to be read at least once
logarithmic time needs halving; summing must visit each item

problems.hint: How many times is each element touched?
problems.explanation: Each of the n elements is read once, so the cost is O(n).

problems.prompt: A loop runs n times, and inside it a second loop also runs n times. What is the Big-O time complexity of the whole thing?

signatures.note: nested loops multiply their costs; they do not add

problems.hint: Nested loops multiply: the inner loop runs fully for every pass of the outer loop.
problems.explanation: n passes of the outer loop times n passes of the inner loop is n * n = O(n^2).

problems.prompt: What is the Big-O complexity of f(n) = 3n^2 + 5n + 20?

signatures.note: dropped the dominant term; the fastest-growing term decides
Big-O drops constants and lower-order terms

problems.hint: Keep only the fastest-growing term and drop its constant.
problems.explanation: The dominant term is 3n^2; dropping the constant gives O(n^2).

problems.prompt: A program runs a binary search, which costs log n steps, once for each of n items. What is the total Big-O time complexity?

signatures.note: ignored the log n cost of each search
the search runs n times, so the costs multiply
a binary search costs log n, not n

problems.hint: Per-item cost times number of items.
problems.explanation: n items, each costing log n, gives n * log n = O(n log n).

binary_search.title: Binary Search
binary_search.objective: Run binary search by hand and explain why it needs sorted data and O(log n) steps.
binary_search.query: binary search sorted halving mid index logarithmic

problems.prompt: Binary search needs the list to be in what condition? Answer in one or two words.

signatures.note: halving is only justified when the list is sorted

problems.hint: Why is it safe to throw away half of the list after one comparison?
problems.explanation: The list must be sorted; otherwise discarding half of it could throw away the target.

problems.prompt: How many times can you halve a list of 16 elements before only one element remains?

signatures.note: that is one halving; keep halving until one element remains
that is a linear scan, not repeated halving

problems.hint: 16, 8, 4, ... keep going until you reach 1.
problems.explanation: 16 -> 8 -> 4 -> 2 -> 1 is 4 halvings (log base 2 of 16).

problems.prompt: Binary search runs on the sorted list [2, 5, 8, 12, 16, 23, 38] looking for 23. With 0-indexed positions, mid = (lo + hi) // 2, lo = 0 and hi = 6, what is the index of the first element compared?

signatures.note: gave the value stored at index 3; the question asks for the index
binary search starts in the middle, not at the front
binary search starts in the middle, not at the end

problems.hint: Plug lo = 0 and hi = 6 into the mid formula.
problems.explanation: mid = (0 + 6) // 2 = 3, and the value at index 3 is 12.

problems.prompt: About how many comparisons does binary search need in the worst case on a sorted list of 1000000 elements? Compute log base 2 of the size and round up to a whole number.

signatures.note: rounded down; 2^19 = 524288 is less than 1000000
that is a linear scan, not binary search
that halves only once instead of repeatedly

problems.hint: 2^10 = 1024, so 2^20 is about a million.
problems.explanation: log2(1000000) is about 19.93, which rounds up to 20 comparisons.

merge_sort.title: Merge Sort
merge_sort.objective: Merge sorted lists by hand and explain why merge sort costs O(n log n).
merge_sort.query: merge sort divide conquer merge sorted halves levels

problems.prompt: Merge sort splits a list of 8 elements all the way down to single-element pieces. How many single-element pieces are there?

signatures.note: gave the number of levels, not the number of pieces
pairs still contain two elements; keep splitting down to single elements

problems.hint: Every element ends up alone.
problems.explanation: Each of the 8 elements ends up in its own piece, so there are 8 pieces (over 3 levels of splitting).

problems.prompt: Merge the sorted lists [1, 4, 6] and [2, 3, 7] into one sorted list.
problems.format: Enter the merged list separated by commas.

signatures.note: concatenated the lists instead of merging by comparing fronts

problems.hint: Repeatedly take the smaller of the two front elements.
problems.explanation: Compare fronts: 1, then 2, then 3, then 4, then 6, then 7 gives [1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7].

problems.prompt: What is the worst-case Big-O time complexity of merge sort?

signatures.note: quadratic is the worst case for simple sorts, not for merge sort
there are log n levels of merging, each doing O(n) work
every element must be handled at every level

problems.hint: How many levels of merging are there, and how much work does each level do?
problems.explanation: log n levels of merging, each doing O(n) work: O(n log n).

problems.prompt: Merge sort on 8 elements has 3 levels of merging, and each level does 8 units of work. How many units of work in total?

signatures.note: added the levels to the work per level; the costs multiply
squared n instead of multiplying n by the number of levels

problems.hint: Work per level times number of levels.
problems.explanation: 3 levels * 8 units per level = 24 units of work.
